tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a monthly solids inventory and mass balance check.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: month end process audit covering aeration, clarifiers, wasting, and solids handling.

cards.label: Total the effluent suspended solids mass discharged during the month
File the balance with the monthly operations report for supervisor review
Total the influent suspended solids mass received during the month
Measure the solids inventory held in the aeration trains and clarifiers at month end
Total the solids mass wasted to solids processing during the month
Reconcile received mass against discharged, wasted, and inventory change and investigate any large gap

tasks.explanation: All four mass terms must be totalled before they can be reconciled, and investigation of a gap precedes filing the report.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for lowering the return sludge rate when clarifier blankets are falling and mixed liquor is too high.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: secondary clarifier blankets are thin, mixed liquor is above target, wasting is already at its normal rate.

cards.label: Reduce the return sludge rate in one small step
Log the new return rate and the blanket response for the next shift
Sample mixed liquor again to confirm the inventory is moving toward target
Watch blanket depth and clarifier effluent clarity over the next few hours
Confirm blanket depth and mixed liquor concentration with fresh samples
Check that wasting is running at the intended rate and the waste line is clear

tasks.explanation: The condition is confirmed and wasting is ruled out before return rate changes, the change is made in one step, and its effect is proven before it is logged.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for establishing a new solids retention time target after a process study.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a two week process study is complete and the supervisor has approved a revised target range.

cards.label: Brief all shifts on the new target and the wasting changes it requires
Summarize study results for effluent quality, settling, and energy use at each trial target
Update the process control sheet and the trending charts with the new target range
Present the recommended target range to the operations team for review
Run the plant at the new target for a trial period with daily review
Confirm the target at the end of the trial or return it to the supervisor for revision

tasks.explanation: Evidence is summarized before a recommendation is made, crews are briefed before the target changes, and a monitored trial confirms the target before it becomes routine.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a spring thaw readiness check before runoff reaches the plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: snowmelt and rain expected within two weeks at a western Canadian plant.

cards.label: Clear snow and ice from access roads, hatches, and chemical delivery points
Confirm chemical and fuel inventories will cover a two week high flow period
Log the readiness check and any item still outstanding for the supervisor
Brief all shifts on flow triggers for extra staffing and sampling
Check standby pumps, generators, and fuel supplies by test running them
Review wet weather procedures and confirm all clarifiers and screens are available

tasks.explanation: Capacity is proven by test runs before it is needed, access and inventories are secured, and briefing aligns every shift on the triggers.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for correcting a slow drift in mixed liquor caused by a faulty solids meter reading.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: online solids readings have drifted below laboratory results for several days, wasting decisions used the online values.

cards.label: Return the meter to service once readings agree within the plant tolerance
Recalibrate the meter and verify it against fresh laboratory samples
Take the online meter out of service for cleaning and calibration checks
Compare online solids readings with paired laboratory grab results over several days
Review wasting records for the drift period and note the correction in the process log
Base wasting decisions on laboratory results while the meter is out of service

tasks.explanation: Drift is proven by paired samples before the meter is removed, laboratory control bridges the gap, and verification precedes the return to service.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for preparing a seasonal solids retention time changeover briefing.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: spring warm up, the plant moves from the winter target to the summer target over two weeks.

cards.label: Review progress at the end of week one and adjust the remaining steps if needed
Calculate the wasting increase needed to move from the winter to the summer inventory
Post the schedule at the control panel and update the target on the trending chart
Make the first scheduled wasting change and confirm blankets stay in range
Draft the two week step down schedule with a wasting change every few days
Brief all shifts on the schedule, the reason for it, and the effluent checks required

tasks.explanation: The schedule is calculated and briefed before any change is made, the first step is proven in the clarifiers, and a mid course review guards the rest of the changeover.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for running a sludge volume index test as part of the weekly control program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: settleability testing on mixed liquor from each aeration train.

cards.label: Plot the results on the control chart and flag any train outside the target band
Collect a fresh mixed liquor sample from each train at the same point in the aeration cycle
Calculate the sludge volume index from the settled volume and the solids result
Mix each sample gently and fill the settleometer to the mark without delay
Record the settled sludge volume at 30 minutes for each sample
Take a paired sample for mixed liquor suspended solids analysis

tasks.explanation: Settled volume and solids must come from paired samples before the index can be calculated, and charting closes the test so trends are visible.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a microscopic examination of mixed liquor.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: routine weekly microscopy to assess biomass health and filament levels.

cards.label: Scan the slide at low power to assess floc size and structure
Record the observations and any process implication in the microscopy log
Scan at higher power to identify indicator organisms and estimate filament abundance
Prepare a wet mount slide with a coverslip and no air bubbles
Collect a fresh mixed liquor sample and bring it to the laboratory promptly
Compare the findings with the previous examination and the settling test results

tasks.explanation: Floc structure is assessed before fine detail, findings are compared with settling behaviour, and the record links the examination to process decisions.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for running an oxygen uptake rate test on mixed liquor.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: respirometry style check using a dissolved oxygen meter and a sealed bottle, values supplied by the lab sheet.

cards.label: Record the rate and any follow up action in the process control log
Insert the dissolved oxygen probe and seal the bottle with no headspace air
Compare the uptake rate with the plant normal range for the current loading
Plot the readings and determine the rate of oxygen decline
Record dissolved oxygen at timed intervals as the biomass consumes oxygen
Collect mixed liquor and aerate it to near saturation in the test bottle

tasks.explanation: The sample must start saturated and sealed before decline can be measured, the rate comes from the plotted decline, and comparison with the normal range gives it meaning.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for completing a dissolved oxygen profile across an aeration basin.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: plug flow aeration basin with sample points at the inlet, middle, and outlet.

cards.label: Measure and record dissolved oxygen and temperature at the inlet point
Calibrate the portable dissolved oxygen meter in air saturated water
Sketch the profile and compare it with the target pattern for the basin
Adjust air distribution or note the needed repair if one zone is far off target
Measure and record dissolved oxygen and temperature at the outlet point
Measure and record dissolved oxygen and temperature at the mid basin point

tasks.explanation: The meter is calibrated before any reading is trusted, the profile follows the flow path, and adjustment follows comparison with the target pattern.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for profiling sludge blanket depth across a secondary clarifier.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: circular secondary clarifier, blanket readings taken at several points from centre to edge.

cards.label: Compare the depths to find any uneven or rising zone
Adjust return rate or flow split as directed by the supervisor
Lower the core sampler slowly at the first point and record the blanket depth
Repeat the measurement at each marked point around the clarifier
Repeat the profile after the adjustment to confirm the blanket has evened out
Check return sludge flow and distribution if one side carries a deeper blanket

tasks.explanation: A full profile precedes any diagnosis, equipment checks follow the pattern found, and a repeat profile proves the adjustment worked.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a centrifuge spin test used to estimate waste sludge concentration.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: quick field estimate to guide wasting before laboratory solids results return.

cards.label: Balance the centrifuge with an equal tube opposite the sample
Convert the reading to an estimated concentration using the plant correlation chart
Spin the sample for the standard time on the lab method sheet
Mix the waste sludge sample thoroughly and fill the centrifuge tube to the mark
Use the estimate for the wasting decision and file the laboratory result when it arrives
Read the compacted solids volume from the tube graduations

tasks.explanation: The tube must be balanced before spinning, the reading is converted with the plant correlation, and the laboratory result later confirms the field estimate.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for setting up a 30 minute settling test series during a bulking investigation.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: suspected filamentous bulking, settling samples taken every two hours for one shift.

cards.label: Note aeration, return rate, and any load changes alongside each result
Plot the series and compare the pattern with microscopy findings
Summarize the series for the supervisor with a recommended next step
Record settled volume and supernatant clarity at the end of each test
Collect and test further samples at the set interval through the shift
Collect the first mixed liquor sample and start the 30 minute settling test

tasks.explanation: Timed tests and operating notes are collected together so cause can be matched to effect, and the plotted series supports the recommendation.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for checking aeration basin foam and assigning a likely cause category.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: brown foam building on one aeration train, effluent quality still in range.

cards.label: Review recent wasting, solids retention time, and load records for changes
Assign the most likely cause category and the matching control action
Collect a foam and mixed liquor sample for microscopic examination
Compare the foam type and records with the plant foam troubleshooting guide
Monitor foam coverage daily and record whether the action is working
Observe and photograph the foam colour, texture, and coverage on each train

tasks.explanation: Observation and microscopy come before record review, the guide match assigns the cause, and daily monitoring tests whether the chosen action works.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for verifying an online dissolved oxygen probe against a bench check.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: basin probe readings differ from operator observations, portable meter available.

cards.label: Clean the probe membrane and check its calibration if the difference is beyond tolerance
Take a mixed liquor sample beside the basin probe location
Compare the portable reading with the control room value for the basin probe
Measure the sample at once with the calibrated portable meter
Log both readings and the maintenance performed for the trending record
Recheck the probe against the portable meter after cleaning or calibration

tasks.explanation: A side by side sample gives a fair comparison, cleaning precedes recalibration, and the recheck proves the probe before its readings are trusted again.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for running a chlorine demand style jar check on final effluent before a disinfection change.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: supervisor wants effluent demand data before changing the disinfection dose setpoint.

cards.label: Measure the residual in each portion at the end of the contact time
Plot dose against residual and report the demand to the supervisor
Collect a fresh final effluent sample before the disinfection point
Dose each portion with a different chlorine dose from the prepared series
Hold the portions for the standard contact time in the dark
Divide the sample into the set of test portions in clean glassware

tasks.explanation: Portions must be dosed as a series and held for the same contact time before residuals are compared, and the plotted demand informs the setpoint decision.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a weekly clarifier performance check using effluent turbidity and solids.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: each secondary clarifier checked in turn while all remain in service.

cards.label: Record blanket depth and return rate for each clarifier at sampling time
Measure turbidity on each sample and submit paired samples for suspended solids
Collect effluent samples from each clarifier at the same time of day
Investigate the poorest clarifier for distribution, blanket, or drive problems
Record the comparison and any work order raised in the process log
Compare clarity and solids between clarifiers at similar loading

tasks.explanation: Samples are comparable only when taken together with operating data, comparison identifies the outlier, and investigation follows the evidence.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for trending process control results at the end of each week.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: operator updates all control charts before the weekly operations meeting.

cards.label: Mark any result outside the target band and note the operating conditions that day
Present the charts and flags at the weekly operations meeting
Enter each result on its control chart in date order
Flag any three day trend moving toward a limit for discussion at the meeting
Calculate the weekly averages used in the operations report
Gather the week of results for solids, settling, dissolved oxygen, and effluent quality

tasks.explanation: Charts are completed before averages are calculated, trends are flagged from the completed charts, and the meeting receives the full picture.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for starting up an anaerobic digester after it has been emptied for inspection.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: primary digester cleaned and repaired, seed sludge available from the second digester.

cards.label: Transfer seed sludge from the operating digester to about one third of the working volume
Monitor volatile acids, alkalinity, and gas production daily until feeding reaches the normal rate
Begin heating and gentle mixing and confirm temperature is rising steadily
Start feeding raw sludge at a low rate once the seed is warm and active
Inspect the digester, mixers, and gas piping and remove all tools and debris
Close and secure all access openings and confirm gas valves are lined up safely

tasks.explanation: The vessel is proven empty and sealed before seed is added, heat and mixing establish activity before feeding starts, and daily chemistry guards the ramp up.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a daily anaerobic digester operating check.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: heated, mixed primary digester in normal service at a western Canadian plant.

cards.label: Log all readings and report any abnormal value to the supervisor the same day
Compare volatile acids to alkalinity information when laboratory results return
Record feed volume, feed solids, and supernatant withdrawal for the previous day
Check gas production, gas pressure, and flare or boiler operation
Sample digested sludge and note appearance, odour, and pH
Record digester temperature and heating system operation

tasks.explanation: Temperature, feed, and gas are the daily vital signs, laboratory chemistry follows sampling, and abnormal values are escalated the same day they appear.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for responding when the volatile acids to alkalinity ratio rises in a digester.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: laboratory reports a rising ratio over three samples, gas production is starting to fall.

cards.label: Review recent feed changes for a sudden increase in volatile solids loading
Reduce the raw sludge feed rate in one controlled step
Hold any increase in feed and check digester temperature for a heating fault
Resample and track the ratio every day or two until it returns to the normal band
Restore the feed rate gradually once the ratio and gas production are stable
Confirm the result by checking the sample dates and requesting a repeat sample

tasks.explanation: The result is confirmed before feed is cut, temperature is ruled out as a cause, and feed returns only gradually after stability is proven by resampling.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for withdrawing supernatant from a digester without disturbing digestion.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: supernatant layer has built up and digester working volume is reduced.

cards.label: Check the sight glass or sample ports to locate the supernatant layer depth
Line up the supernatant valve to return flow to the plant inlet at a controlled rate
Open the withdrawal valve slowly and watch the returned flow for solids carryover
Note the returned load in the log so the next shift expects the added flow
Record the volume withdrawn and the layer depth remaining
Close the valve if the draw turns dark with solids

tasks.explanation: The layer is located before any valve opens, withdrawal stops at the first sign of solids, and the log warns the next shift about the returned load.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for transferring digested sludge from the primary to the secondary digester.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: primary digester level is high, secondary digester has available capacity.

cards.label: Check levels in both digesters and confirm the transfer line is lined up
Stop the pump and close the transfer valves in order
Record volumes, levels, and pump run time in the solids log
Start the transfer pump at a low rate and check for leaks along the line
Transfer the planned volume while watching the primary level fall
Sample the secondary digester if a digestion check is due

tasks.explanation: Levels and lineup come before pumping, the transfer is watched while it runs, and records close the move so inventories stay accurate.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for investigating a sudden drop in digester gas production.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: gas meter shows production well below the recent average for two days.

cards.label: Reduce feed if chemistry shows stress, following supervisor direction
Log the findings and the corrective action and trend gas daily until normal
Check digester temperature and heating records for a loss of heat
Review feed records for a drop in volume or volatile solids fed
Request volatile acids and alkalinity tests on a fresh digester sample
Verify the gas meter reading and check the gas line and condensate trap for blockage

tasks.explanation: Metering and feed are checked before biology is blamed, chemistry confirms stress before feed is cut, and daily trending proves recovery.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for preparing a digester for a planned mixing system repair.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one mixer out of service for repair, digester stays in operation on the remaining mixers.

cards.label: Confirm gas piping and pressure relief remain in normal service
Reduce the feed rate to match the lower mixing capacity
Isolate and lock out only the mixer being repaired
Notify the supervisor and maintenance of the repair window and the operating limits
Support maintenance with level and temperature information during the repair
Return the mixer to service, restore normal mixing, and raise feed back in steps

tasks.explanation: Feed is matched to reduced mixing before work starts, only the affected mixer is isolated, and feed returns in steps after mixing is restored.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a monthly volatile solids reduction calculation for the digestion process.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: month end reporting, feed and digested sludge solids results are available.

cards.label: Account for any change in volatile solids inventory stored in the digesters
Total the volatile solids mass leaving in digested sludge during the month
Total the volatile solids mass fed to the digesters during the month
Compare the result with the plant target and note any explanation in the monthly report
Calculate percent volatile solids reduction from the mass destroyed and the mass fed
Calculate the mass destroyed as fed mass minus leaving mass adjusted for inventory

tasks.explanation: Fed, leaving, and inventory terms must all be totalled before destruction can be calculated, and the percentage follows from those masses.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for handling digester foaming that is lifting the cover pressure.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: foam suspected from rising gas pressure and foam at the sample port, feeding continues.

cards.label: Review feed sludge for a change in character or a high strength delivery
Confirm foam presence at the sample port and check gas pressure readings
Apply only the supervisor approved foam control measure if foam persists
Check mixing operation and restart any mixer found out of service
Reduce the feed rate and stop any recent feed increase that preceded the foam
Monitor pressure and foam daily and record the trend until the event clears

tasks.explanation: Foam is confirmed before feed changes, mixing is restored as a basic control, and approved measures are used only if the basic steps fail.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for warming a cold digester back to its operating temperature after a heating outage.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: heating boiler was down for two days in winter, digester temperature has fallen several degrees.

cards.label: Raise temperature gradually, no faster than the site procedure allows per day
Hold the feed rate low while the digester is below its normal temperature
Monitor volatile acids and alkalinity more often during the warm up
Watch gas production as an early sign that biology is recovering
Return to the normal feed rate once temperature and chemistry are both stable
Confirm the boiler is repaired and the heating loop is circulating

tasks.explanation: Heat is restored before feeding is trusted, temperature rises gradually to protect the biology, and normal feeding waits for stable chemistry.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for sampling a digester for the full monthly laboratory suite.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: samples needed for volatile solids, volatile acids, alkalinity, and metals screening.

cards.label: Label each container with digester, date, time, and sampler initials
Flush the sample line to waste until fresh digested sludge reaches the port
Deliver samples to the laboratory within the holding time on the plan
Fill the laboratory containers in the order on the sample plan, volatile acids first
Record digester temperature and feed conditions at the time of sampling
File the chain of custody copy and note the sampling in the solids log

tasks.explanation: The line is flushed so the sample represents the digester, containers are filled in the planned order, and custody records prove the samples reached the lab on time.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for shutting down an aerobic digester for decanting and cleaning.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: small aerobic digester at a lagoon style western plant, solids to be hauled after decanting.

cards.label: Turn off the aeration blowers to allow the solids to settle
Decant clear supernatant back to the plant inlet once settling is complete
Inspect the aeration grid and walls before the digester returns to service
Open the digester for cleaning once the solids are removed
Stop feeding sludge to the digester and record the last feed date
Sample the settled solids for the hauling and disposal record

tasks.explanation: Feeding stops before settling can begin, decanting waits for settling, and inspection happens while the vessel is empty before it returns to service.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for starting up a belt filter press for a dewatering shift.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: belt press with polymer feed, gravity drainage, and a cake conveyor.

cards.label: Start the cake conveyor and confirm the discharge container is in place
Check cake solids on the first sample and record the start up settings
Start the polymer feed system and confirm flow at the mixing unit
Adjust belt tension and speed once cake is forming evenly
Start the sludge feed pump at a low rate and watch the gravity drainage zone
Inspect the belts, rollers, and wash water system and clear any old cake

tasks.explanation: Containment and polymer are ready before sludge arrives, the press loads gradually, and the first cake sample proves the settings.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for optimizing polymer dose during a dewatering run.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: cake is wetter than usual and filtrate clarity has fallen during the run.

cards.label: Reduce or raise the polymer dose in one small step as directed by the test results
Collect fresh cake and filtrate samples at the new dose
Compare cake dryness and filtrate clarity between the two doses
Allow the press to run long enough for the change to reach the cake discharge
Settle on the best dose, record it, and note the feed solids it applies to
Collect cake and filtrate samples at the current polymer dose

tasks.explanation: Samples at the old dose give the baseline, one step changes at a time, and comparison of paired samples selects the dose.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for shutting down and washing a belt filter press at the end of a run.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: planned end of run, press will stand idle until the next dewatering day.

cards.label: Stop the belts and the wash water and release belt tension if the procedure requires it
Stop the sludge feed pump and let the remaining sludge clear the belts
Run the belts with wash water on until both belts are clean
Empty and wash the press area floor and the filtrate sump
Stop the polymer feed and flush the polymer lines with water
Log the run hours, cake produced, and any belt damage noticed

tasks.explanation: Feed stops before polymer so the belts clear in order, washing happens while the belts still run, and the log captures condition for the next run.
